newsitem.title: SPAIN: Upside seen for Metrovacesa after results.
newsitem.headline: Upside seen for Metrovacesa after results.

text.p: Shares in Spanish property group Metrovacesa traded below an intraday high on Wednesday after nine-month results met market forecasts, but dealers saw more upside for the shares in the next few months.
At 1105 GMT, Metrovacesa was up 15 pesetas, 0.34 percent, to 4,465 compared with a session high of 4,490. The Ibex-35 index was up 0.01 percent to 4,352.61.
Metrovacesa posted a 10.6 percent rise in net profit to September, with rental income up 17.2 percent.

"I don't think the results are especially positive in the sense that they're in line with what people were expecting, but we think that they're going to be doing pretty well in the future," said Ignacio Rodriguez, a dealer at Benito y Monjardin brokerage in Madrid.
"It's trading at a large (41 percent) discount to net asset value and we think that will fall to around 30 percent."
B&M's 1996 target price for Metrovacesa is 4,900 pesetas.
The dealer highlighted that Metrovacesa had succeeded in its aim of increasing property sales substantially while maintaining a tight control over operating costs.
The firm's sales rose 55.5 percent in the first nine months of the year while operating costs increased 1.2 percent.
